assumptions: The initial business is limited to Poland or nearby CEE markets and begins with one or very few named commercial inverter cohorts.
The founder may obtain lawful pilot introductions through the family renewable-energy company but receives no free inventory, exclusive supply, or ownership of its customers.
Inventory is purchased only after a cohort census and paid commitments, and qualified electricians remain responsible for diagnosis and installation.
No current supplier warranty, repurchase right, minimum-volume customer contract, or proven interchangeability can be assumed.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Obtain a serial-number-level census for at least several installer or O&M portfolios; model-specific failure, repair, lead-time, and downtime-cost records; certified compatibility and test procedures; documented authentic supply with landed costs and write-down terms; and signed paid reservations whose cohort revenue covers inventory, support, warranty, and expected losses under conservative failure scenarios.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The mismatch between long-lived PV assets and shorter or discontinued inverter support cycles is a credible source of downtime, and converting scarce spares into a cohort-specific availability promise is more disciplined than generic parts trading. However, the supplied evidence concerns PV modules or system lifetime generally and does not establish which inverter cohorts are scarce, failure-prone, or economically worth reserving.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Commercial PV downtime, emergency sourcing, and forced repowering can create real monetary loss, so an enforceable response-time commitment can be valuable. The current packet provides no model-level outage duration, lost-production value, stockout record, insurance requirement, paid reservation, or evidence that customers prefer an annual reserve fee to repair, replacement, or self-held spares.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Prepaid reservations could improve cash conversion and narrow cohort selection can constrain inventory, but the proposed 300-1200 PLN annual fee is not tied to failure frequency, unit cost, write-down risk, testing cadence, warranty returns, storage, channel share, or SLA liability. Hardware margins are modest, capital can remain trapped for years, and the claimed 35-55% reservation contribution margin and twelve-month inventory payback are unsupported.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: A single regional installer portfolio and one named unsupported inverter family form a testable beachhead, while Poland's large PV installed base creates a future equipment-aging pool. Yet much of the Polish micro-PV fleet was installed only from 2019 onward, the candidate does not size the relevant commercial cohorts, and narrowing enough to manage technical risk may leave too few homogeneous systems to support a reserve.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Local possession of tested units plus a contractual dispatch time could beat ad hoc sourcing in a narrow cohort. Nonetheless, established European providers already advertise inverter component repair, maintenance contracts, refurbished inventory, spare parts, and replacement procurement, while OEMs, distributors, and large O&M firms control stronger supply and customer relationships; no exclusive supply or contracted fleet is secured.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful cohort can extend to adjacent inverter families, boards, adapters, batteries, insurers, O&M portfolios, and additional CEE regions, with observed failures improving inventory selection. Each expansion also adds certification, compatibility, inventory, and working-capital complexity, so adjacency is plausible but not automatically high-leverage.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Serial-numbered inventory, compatibility records, failure data, and embedded fleet SLAs could form a modest operational moat. The inventory is purchasable by competitors, customer switching costs are low before a binding portfolio contract, data compounds slowly at low failure rates, and the scarcity premium can disappear when repair, adapters, compatible replacements, or OEM supply improve.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A verified same-day or next-day swap can be materially faster and safer than searching after failure, especially for a high-value site. No evidence yet quantifies the promised response advantage, compatibility success rate, or total cost advantage over existing repair and replacement channels, and a refund does not compensate an owner for uncovered downtime.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Poland's rapid PV buildout creates a foreseeable wave of aging electronics and EU solar expansion enlarges the eventual service base. The near-term legacy window is uncertain because much of the fleet is young, and the cited EU installation policy supports new capacity rather than present scarcity of particular inverter models.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: The family installation company provides a lawful, low-cost route to census a small fleet and test an installer-mediated offer without personal-brand selling. Scaling requires many installers or O&M partners to share accurate fleet data and sell a new annual fee, while those partners currently own the relationship and can internalize the reserve or use existing European channels.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A tightly bounded pilot fits the founder's analytical skills, part-time schedule, and 100,000 PLN capital ceiling, with electricians handling field work. Reliable diagnosis, electrical safety, provenance, firmware and grid-code compatibility, liability, warranty, refurbishment quality, logistics, and disposal require specialist processes; inventory errors can consume the full capital budget before demand is proven.

highest_value_structural_change: Make the offer a prepaid, cohort-specific B2B fleet-uptime contract with minimum covered-unit commitments and supplier consignment, repurchase, or purchase-option terms, so customer revenue covers each inventory cohort before capital is deployed and obsolete-stock risk is shared rather than borne entirely by the founder.
main_structural_strength: A narrowly selected, physically controlled stock of tested replacements can turn an unpredictable sourcing problem into a measurable uptime SLA, while the fleet census and dispatch history improve subsequent capital allocation.
primary_score_limiter: There is no evidence that any sufficiently large homogeneous cohort combines frequent or costly failures, genuine replacement scarcity, and reservation willingness at a price that covers inventory write-downs and SLA delivery.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Established European providers already offer component-level inverter repair, maintenance contracts, stocked parts, refurbished inverter sales, and replacement procurement; this weakens the claim that a new regional reserve has a uniquely unavailable supply solution, while the candidate's own IEA sources do not document inverter-model scarcity.
